props.title: Turn the dial
props.expect: In Claude Code, press **Shift+Tab** a few times and watch the mode's name change: manual, accept edits, plan, auto. Then type `/rewind` to see your checkpoints, and choose **Never mind** to leave without changing anything.

steps.title: What needs a call
steps.text: A house-sitter has a list: some things they just do, others they call you about first. Claude Code's list is its **permission mode**: what Claude may do without asking you.

steps.title: Settings on a dial
steps.text: **Manual**: Claude asks before editing a file or running most commands. **Accept edits**: it edits files without asking. **Plan**: it reads and proposes a plan, changing nothing. Press **Shift+Tab** to switch.

steps.title: Auto is the default
steps.text: As of October 2026, new terminal sessions start in **auto** mode: instead of asking you, a second model checks most actions in the background. Like Claude, that checker is probabilistic.

steps.title: You're still the reviewer
steps.text: Fewer questions doesn't mean less responsibility: Claude Code's documentation says you're responsible for reviewing what Claude proposes. Read the actions it lists, not just its summary.

steps.title: Every prompt, a checkpoint
steps.text: Each prompt you send saves a **checkpoint**: the files Claude is about to edit, as they were. Type `/rewind`, or press Esc twice, to go back and restore the files, the conversation, or both.

steps.title: What it can't undo
steps.text: Checkpoints track only edits made with Claude's own file-editing tools. A file changed by a command, like `mv` or `rm`, isn't tracked, and nobody can unsend an email: actions on outside systems are governed by your permission mode, not by undo.

steps.title: Git: the long-term save
steps.text: Checkpoints are for quick undo inside a session. For lasting history, use **git**: each **commit** is a labelled snapshot of your folder, like a photo album of past versions. Ask Claude to commit when a piece of work is done.

steps.title: The whole picture
steps.text: Your permission mode decides what happens without asking. Checkpoints undo Claude's file edits; git keeps every version you commit. Nothing undoes what has left your computer, so that's where to stay strict.
